text: 🇲🇽🏭 Mexico is turning invasive Caribbean sargassum into rural roads. The fibers in sargassum absorb tension — making them ideal for stabilizing the base layers of community-built "caminos artesanales." Already in pilot use by the Instituto Mexicano del Transporte. — Jesús Esteva Medina, Secretary of Infrastructure, Mañanera 03/06/2026 In 2026: 6 billion pesos for 388 artisanal roads built in assembly with Indigenous communities across 18 states. Program also uses recovered tire rubber. One invasive species, two solutions: clearing Caribbean coasts + connecting remote villages.

🇲🇽✊ "I was paying 8,000 pesos in rent. Now I pay 4,000 — and the house is mine." Erika Adriana Zaragoza Sánchez, mother of three engineers, received the keys to her new 60-square-meter home at Parques del Triunfo in El Salto, Jalisco — Mexico's electronics manufacturing corridor. — Beneficiary, Programa de Vivienda del Bienestar, 03/06/2026 It was the 25th "Miércoles de Vivienda." 87 developments active nationwide, 21,500 families housed. 13 more open in June. Jalisco's goal raised from 29,500 to 75,743 units; 45.5 billion pesos invested.

🇲🇽⚖️ Mexico just made foreign election interference a constitutional cause for annulment. Published yesterday in the Diario Oficial. Article 41 of the Constitution now permits federal or local elections to be voided when proven foreign interference influenced the result. — Consejera Jurídica Luisa María Alcalde, Mañanera 03/06/2026 Proposed by Morena's Ricardo Monreal. Passed both chambers and 25 state congresses. In favor: Morena, PT, Green Party. Against: PAN, PRI, Movimiento Ciudadano. Secondary laws to define evidentiary standards within 90 days.

🇲🇽🌎 Migrant encounters at the US southern border: down 97.5%. From 305,608 monthly encounters in December 2023 — the historic peak under Biden — to 5,433 in May 2026. Daily average so far this year: 271. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera 03/06/2026, citing CBP data The chart was built from US Customs and Border Protection's own numbers. The reduction came without militarizing the border or surrendering sovereignty — through south-to-south development, humanitarian management, and coordination with origin countries.

🚨🇲🇽 "We cannot accept calling these groups terrorists." On the US designation of Mexican cartels as foreign terrorist organizations: "Terrorist groups have a different objective: they seek to overthrow governments and harm civilians for a concrete political end. These groups are criminal — but not terrorists. The United States has always used drug trafficking to intervene in Mexico." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera 03/06/2026 After Washington's terrorist designation, Mexico amended its Constitution to prohibit any foreign interference in security operations. Homicides under this administration: down 40%.

🚨🇲🇽 "What's the intent in pulling a visa — and leaking it?" Washington stripped the US visas of Mexican governors Alfonso Durazo (Sonora) and Américo Villarreal (Tamaulipas), then leaked it to the press: "They have to explain. What's the intent in pulling the visa and making it public — to warn Mexicans their visas will be pulled? The people put leaders in. The people take them out." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera 03/06/2026 This week, Mexico published a constitutional reform allowing annulment of any election where foreign interference is proven. The public visa leak as political signal is exactly what the reform was written for.

🚨🇲🇽 "We are not Díaz Ordaz." Asked if she would meet CNTE teachers' union leaders amid protests, with the World Cup weeks away: "They want us to fall into repression on the eve of the World Cup. We won't. We are not Díaz Ordaz. The dialogue stays open to work on the teachers' issues." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera 03/06/2026 In 1968, ten days before the Olympics, President Díaz Ordaz ordered the Tlatelolco massacre — hundreds of students and teachers killed. The current government refuses that path.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>USTR PROPOSES 10% FORCED-LABOR TARIFF ON MEXICO — ECONOMY SAYS 85% OF EXPORTS ARE TMEC-COMPLIANT AND ALREADY EXEMPT</u>

The US Trade Representative opened forced-labor investigations against 60 economies, proposing a 10% tariff on Mexico (and 13 others) plus 12.5% on 46 more. Mexico's Economy Ministry response: roughly 85% of Mexican exports to the US comply with TMEC rules of origin and are therefore exempt from the proposed measure.

Deadlines: June 22 to register testimony, July 6 for written comments. A formal negotiation round inside the TMEC review is locked in for the coming weeks.

Mexico isn't waiting to be punished. It's showing up at the desk with the paperwork already done.

Source: El Economista

🇺🇸🇮🇷 <u>US STRIKES IRANIAN ISLAND OF QESHM — CEASEFIRE BROKEN, PEACE TALKS HALT</u>

CENTCOM bombed an IRGC ground-control station on Qeshm Island today, claiming it intercepted Iranian missiles and drones aimed at Kuwait and Bahrain. CENTCOM statement: "American forces responded with strikes on Qeshm Island. No U.S. personnel or assets were damaged."

The IRGC said it hit the US 5th Fleet center in Bahrain and an airbase in retaliation. The 60-day extended ceasefire — the one Vance pushed last month — is effectively over. Indirect peace talks have halted; Trump's "deal in days" line has expired.

26 ships through Hormuz yesterday. The blockade still isn't holding.

Source: Regeneración
